title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 14: distinguish electing act from eternal life elected — dispositive vs motive
pass_a_gloss: Solution. That this argument may be rightly solved, a distinction must be made between the action itself of God electing to eternal life, and the thing itself to which he elects, that is, eternal life itself. For something can have the force of a dispositive cause with respect to the production of the thing, which had no force of a motive cause with respect to the intention of the one electing. We do not deny that good works, or a holy and pious life, in that manner work toward the attainment of eternal life, and that God from eternity looked upon this holy life of the elect as preceding their entrance into the heavenly kingdom.
pass_b_english: Sol. To solve this rightly, distinguish God's act of electing to eternal life from the thing elected — eternal life itself. What can be a dispositive cause of producing the thing need not have been a motive cause of the elector's intention. We do not deny that good works, or a holy and pious life, work that way toward attaining eternal life, and that God from eternity looked on the elect's holy life as preceding their entrance into the heavenly kingdom.
source_text: Sol. Ut hoc argumentum recte solvatur, distinguendum est inter ipsam actionem Dei eligentis ad vitam aeternam, et ipsam rem ad quam eligit, hoc est, ipsam vitam aeternam. Potest enim habere vim causae dispositivae quoad productionem rei, quod nullam habuit vim causae motivae quoad intentionem eligentis. Non imus inficias, bona opera, sive vitam sanctam et piam, isto modo operari ad consecutionem vitae aeternae, atque Deum ab aeterno intuitum fuisse hanc electorum sanctam vitam, tanquam praecedaneam ad illorum introitum in regnum caeleste.
